articles.title: Rupee soars 69 paise to settle at its eight-month high of 92.16 against US dollar
articles.excerpt:
The rupee on Wednesday jumped 69 paise to settle at 92.16 (provisional), the highest level in this year so far, drawing cues from robust buying in domestic equity markets and unabated foreign fund inflows.

Lower crude oil prices also helped the local currency pare all its losses of the current financial year while investors worldwide preferred Indian equities over other assets, forex traders said.

At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 92.65 and peaked to 92.16 (provisional) against the greenback at the end of the session, up 69 paise from its previous close.

articles.title: LG Electronics shares to be in focus as promoter to sell 2% stake to meet public float norms; check details
articles.excerpt:

The floor price has been set at ₹1,709.30 per share, according to the company's filing.

The offer involves the sale of up to 13.58 million shares, worth up to ₹2,320.5 crore. The promoter will be subject to a 180-day lock-in period, during which it will be restricted from selling any further stake in the company.

articles.excerpt:
(Bloomberg) -- The plunge in the value of Bitcoin is putting pressure on billion-dollar mining companies to liquidate their remaining token reserves, both to cover steep operating costs and to fund an increasingly strained pivot into AI data centers.

A key measure of mining revenue, known as hash price, slumped to its lowest in at least a year as Bitcoin fell to a more than two-year low of around $55,000 last weekend, Hashrate Index data show. articles.title: Card payments edge past cash in shops; euro area consumers want both
articles.excerpt:
The European Central Bank (ECB) today published its latest study on the payment attitudes of consumers in the euro area (SPACE). The results show that consumers are increasingly using digital means of payment, while cash continues to play an important role.

For the first time since comparable data were collected in 2016,[1] cards were used more often than cash at physical locations, such as shops. In 2026 cards accounted for 45% of transactions, compared with 44% for cash. Mobile payments increased to 9%, from 6% in 2024.
